extraction.name: Visual Question Answering Datasets Survey
extraction.description: A review paper critically examining the current state of Visual Question Answering (VQA) in terms of problem formulation, existing datasets (DAQUAR, COCO-QA, The VQA Dataset, FM-IQA, Visual7W, Visual Genome, SHAPES), evaluation metrics, and algorithms. The paper discusses limitations of current datasets with regard to their ability to properly train and assess VQA algorithms, exhaustively reviews existing algorithms, and discusses possible future directions for VQA and image understanding research.
extraction.creator: Kushal Kafle, Christopher Kanan
extraction.citeAs: Kafle, K. and Kanan, C. (2017). Visual Question Answering: Datasets, Algorithms, and Future Challenges. arXiv:1610.01465v4 [cs.CV].
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Multiple VQA datasets were collected using different methods: DAQUAR used images from NYU-DepthV2 with manual and automated QA pair generation; COCO-QA used an NLP algorithm to derive QA pairs from COCO image captions; The VQA Dataset used Amazon Mechanical Turk workers to generate questions and answers for COCO images and synthetic cartoon images; FM-IQA collected human-generated questions and answers originally in Chinese with English translations; Visual Genome used crowdsourced dense image annotations with both free-form and region-specific question prompting; Visual7W is a subset of Visual Genome with additional pointing questions.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Manual Human Curator, Web Scraping, User-generated content data, Software Collection, Experiments
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: The authors were unable to retrieve the English version of the FM-IQA dataset from the provided download link.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Images sourced from: NYU-DepthV2 Dataset (DAQUAR), Microsoft COCO dataset with 328,000 images (COCO-QA, COCO-VQA, Visual7W), synthetic cartoon scenes (SYNTH-VQA), COCO and YFCC100M/Flickr100M images (Visual Genome). QA pairs were generated from captions, crowdsourced workers, or NLP algorithms applied to existing captions.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: Datasets released beginning in 2014; review covers datasets available as of article publication in 2017.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: For COCO-VQA multiple-choice format, 18 answer choices were constructed comprising: the correct answer (most frequent answer from 10 annotators), 3 plausible answers collected from annotators without seeing the image, top 10 most popular answers in the dataset, and randomly selected correct answers for other questions. For Visual7W pointing questions, multiple-choice options are four plausible bounding boxes. The Yin and Yang dataset was built on top of SYNTH-VQA to eliminate answer biases by creating paired images where the same question has different correct answers.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: For COCO-QA, an NLP algorithm derived QA pairs from COCO image captions by breaking longer sentences into smaller chunks. For Visual Genome, two modes of data collection were used: free-form questions and region-specific questions prompted by descriptive bounding-box annotations. COCO-VQA answers were processed using a consensus-based evaluation metric where the most frequent answer among 10 annotators was used as the correct answer.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: COCO-VQA: Amazon Mechanical Turk workers were asked to 'Stump a smart robot' to generate questions, and a separate pool of workers generated answers; each question was answered by 10 independent annotators. DAQUAR-consensus: an average of five human annotated ground truth answers per question were collected. Visual Genome: annotators asked free-form questions and region-specific questions about images. Visual7W: annotators provided plausible answers by answering questions without seeing the image for multiple-choice distractors. FM-IQA: human-generated questions and answers, originally in Chinese.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: Amazon Mechanical Turk (AMT) for The VQA Dataset (COCO-VQA and SYNTH-VQA).
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Inter-human agreement on COCO-VQA is approximately 83.3% using the AccuracyVQA metric. For 'Why' questions, over 59% have fewer than three annotators giving exactly the same answer. More than 13% of yes/no questions in COCO-VQA have both 'yes' and 'no' repeated by more than three annotators. Answering 'yes' to all yes/no questions yields 71% accuracy due to dataset bias (majority answer is 'yes' 58% of the time). Simple questions can evoke diverse answers from annotators.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: COCO-VQA: 3 questions per image, 10 answers per question. SYNTH-VQA: 3 questions per scene, 10 ground truth answers per question. DAQUAR-consensus: average of 5 human annotated ground truth answers per question. Visual Genome: average of 17 QA pairs per image.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: NLP algorithm used to derive QA pairs from COCO image captions for COCO-QA dataset. Edge Boxes used for bounding box region proposals in some VQA algorithms. Word2vec used for computing similarity between words in questions and object labels.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: SYNTH-VQA synthetic human models span different age, gender, and races to provide variation in appearance.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: VQA has potential applications as an aid to blind and visually impaired individuals, enabling them to get information about images on the web and in the real world. VQA could improve human-computer interaction as a natural way to query visual content, and can be used for image retrieval without using image meta-data or tags.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Language biases are a major problem: question-only models achieve up to 49.6% accuracy on COCO-VQA without using images. Yes/no answers span about 38% of all COCO-VQA questions, with 59% answered 'yes'. Answering 'yes' to all yes/no questions yields 71% accuracy. Questions beginning with 'Is there' can be answered 'yes' with 85.2% accuracy. Harder question types like 'Why' and 'Where' are rare, making overall accuracy metrics misleading. DAQUAR contains exclusively indoor scenes. COCO-QA is limited to four question types derived from captions. Natural image datasets have contextual biases (e.g., street scenes more likely to have dogs than zebras). VQA systems are sensitive to question phrasing, with MCB-ensemble achieving 33.6% for 'What are they doing?' vs 86.4% for 'What sport are they playing?' about the same images.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: DAQUAR is too small to train and evaluate complex models, contains only indoor scenes, and humans achieve only 50.2% accuracy. COCO-QA has grammatical errors and nonsensical questions due to flaws in the NLP generation algorithm, and only has four question types. COCO-VQA contains subjective opinion-seeking questions without single objective answers, and questions that can be answered without the image. FM-IQA requires human judges for evaluation making it impractical for most research groups. Visual Genome's long-tailed answer distribution makes open-ended evaluation challenging. Multiple-choice evaluation allows systems to exploit answer biases rather than truly solving VQA. Current datasets are not sufficient to evaluate whether an algorithm has 'solved' VQA. Training data curves have not approached asymptotes, suggesting datasets are still too small.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, Testing, and Validation of VQA algorithms. Benchmarking visual question answering systems. Evaluating image understanding capabilities. Component of a Visual Turing Test for image understanding. The paper recommends mean per-question-type performance should replace standard accuracy for more meaningful benchmarking.
